reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5 (claude-sonnet-5), this session -- NOT qualified to clear (see output/calibration/reconciliation.json). This is a provisional gap analysis, not an approved curriculum change.
method: Started from references/CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json (a dated aggregate, meta.generatedAt=2026-09-06T18:02:49.683Z, ledgerVersion 3.1.0). Refreshed the core counts against the LIVE composed experimental bank at the pinned sourceCommit f1f5667bc5daa7ac7edae010e36b8c87873e6645 using tools/experimental-bank-files.mjs (readBankFiles). The refresh matched the dated file exactly on every number checked (200 scenarios, 1600 questions, age distribution U7=20/U9=30/U11=50/U13=50/U15=30/U18=20) -- no drift found, so the dated aggregate's counts are current as of this run. Two additional independent checks were run directly against the live bank rather than relying on the aggregate's own domain-signal methodology: (1) a keyword re-scan for skating/edges/agility/pivot/backward/deception content by age band, and (2) a scan for 'Imagine...'/'Suppose...' hypothetical-consequence question prompts by age band. Both are reported below with exact counts and are distinguishable from the dated file's own domain-signal numbers.
explicitCaveat: Per references/CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json's own methodology note: signal counts are 'a signal map from actual scenario tags, topic, family and objective; this is an inventory aid, not an authored concept binding.' Topic-level scenario counts are NOT used as gap evidence here because the bank is designed with ~1:1 scenario-to-family granularity (195 families across 200 scenarios) -- almost every topic shows 'scenarios: 1' by construction, so a low topic count is not itself a gap signal. Only domain-level (6 domains) and age-band-level signals, which aggregate across many scenarios, are used as gap evidence. Delivery-format gaps (true-false, tap-player-feature, pick-spot-lane -- all show currentQuestionCount:0 in the dated file's own formatRows) are explicitly NOT counted as tactical-situation gaps, per the assignment's instruction not to count delivery formats as new tactical situations.

gaps.skillConcept: Skating & Movement domain (edges/balance, agility/mobility, backward transitions, deception-with-feet) -- RinkReads' own domain taxonomy, domains[0] in CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json
gaps.currentEvidenceAndDate: Verified live against the pinned sourceCommit on 2026-09-07: 0 scenes in U15 or U18 match skating/edges/agility/pivot/backward/deception keywords across tags, topic, family or objective (10 total skating-signal scenes exist bank-wide, distributed U7=1, U9=2, U11=3, U13=4, U15=0, U18=0). The dated CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json aggregate reports the same pattern independently via its own domain-signal method (skating-movement domain: 8 signal scenarios, ageBands explicitly listed as only ['U7','U9','U11','U13'] -- U15/U18 absent). Both methods agree; this is not a stale or unmapped-tag artifact.
gaps.missingQuestionFormatsOrCues: No skating/edge-work visible cue (stride length, crossover mechanics, backward-to-forward pivot points, deceptive footwork setup) appears in any U15/U18 scene. Existing question types (choice, multi, position) are sufficient to deliver this content once a scene shows the relevant visible cue; no new delivery format is required.
gaps.developmentalRationale: Hockey Canada's Skating Pathway explicitly frames skating as a skill that continues developing past early specialization, and agility/edge work under game-speed pressure (not just straight-line speed) is a stated emphasis for older, more competitive play. A bank that teaches gap control, angling, forechecking and transition entirely through positional geometry without ever surfacing the skating mechanic that enables those reads leaves a genuine hole at exactly the ages where skating separates players most.

gaps.recommendedSmallPilot: 2 new U15 scenes and 2 new U18 scenes (4 total, 8 questions), each pairing a skating/edge cue (e.g. a tight turn setting up an angling approach, a backward-to-forward pivot before a gap-control read) with the SAME kind of geometry-comparison question already proven throughout this assignment's audit (e.g. 'which line stays farther from X'), so the pilot tests whether skating cues can be added without inventing a new question format.

gaps.skillConcept: Rink landmarks and beginner vocabulary (net, boards, blue line, faceoff circle)
gaps.currentEvidenceAndDate: Carried forward from references/CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json backlogCandidates (dated 2026-09-06). U7 currently has 20 scenarios / 160 questions, topTags include 'blue-line' and 'landmark', but no scenario is built around pure landmark identification as the primary objective -- existing U7 objectives sampled from the file are tactical ('Find a teammate before choosing whom to involve') rather than vocabulary-first.
gaps.missingQuestionFormatsOrCues: The original backlog candidate proposed a 'label-picture / tap-player-feature' delivery format, which does not exist in the current app (formatRows confirms 0 questions of type tap-player-feature bank-wide). This gap plan does NOT propose adding that format; instead it recommends achieving the same landmark-vocabulary objective using the EXISTING 'choice' or 'explain' question types, asking the learner to identify a landmark from the rendered scene by choosing among labeled options.
gaps.developmentalRationale: Hockey Canada's U7 (Timbits) FAQ and game-play-rules pages describe cross-ice, foundational orientation as a stated program priority before tactical reads are meaningful. A player who cannot name the blue line or the faceoff circle cannot use those landmarks in the rink-relative language this bank already requires ('use rink-relative landmarks, not camera-relative directions' -- the exact convention audited throughout this assignment).

gaps.recommendedSmallPilot: 2 new U7 scenes (4 questions) using the existing 'choice' type, each scene showing one clear landmark (net/crease, blue line, faceoff circle) and asking the learner to identify it or a player's position relative to it, using only vocabulary already used elsewhere in the U7 band.

gaps.skillConcept: Passing and receiving while both players are moving (not a static freeze)
gaps.currentEvidenceAndDate: Carried forward from references/CURRICULUM-COVERAGE.json backlogCandidates. U9 has 30 scenarios / 240 questions; every scene in this bank is an explicitly static freeze ('Static original practice illustration; movement and outcomes are not simulated' appears in every scene's limits field, confirmed while reviewing all 60 audited questions in this assignment). This is a structural property of the whole bank, not specific to U9, but the U9 official pathway places unusual emphasis on receiving in motion.
gaps.missingQuestionFormatsOrCues: No new format needed. The gap is a scene-content gap: a freeze showing a receiver mid-stride with one clearly open and one clearly blocked route, using the existing 'choice' or 'position' type.
gaps.developmentalRationale: Hockey Canada's U9 Player Pathway document names passing and receiving, in sequence with skating and puck control, as core age-band emphases. A static-freeze bank can still test 'which route is open right now' without claiming to simulate motion, exactly as the audited packets already do for passing-lane comparisons at older ages -- this pilot would extend that proven pattern down to U9's receiving-specific framing.

gaps.recommendedSmallPilot: 2 new U9 scenes (4 questions) each freezing a receiver a moment before the puck arrives, with one open and one blocked route, asking which route to take -- geometry-comparison pattern already validated in this assignment's audit.

gaps.skillConcept: Named 'cause-and-effect' family: a stated hypothetical action by one actor and the resulting change to the learner's best read (distinct from the existing scattered 'Imagine X...' questions)
gaps.currentEvidenceAndDate: Verified live against the pinned sourceCommit on 2026-09-07: bank-wide, questions whose prompt begins 'Imagine...' or 'Suppose...' (a hypothetical-consequence framing) number 20/160 (12.5%) at U7, 18/240 (7.5%) at U9, 14/400 (3.5%) at U11, 2/400 (0.5%) at U13, 6/240 (2.5%) at U15, 2/160 (1.25%) at U18. U11 sits at a proportional dip relative to the two younger bands despite having the largest scenario count (50) to draw on, and this assignment's own instructions specifically flag U11 as the right age to pilot a named cause-and-effect family 'where supported' -- U11 already has real, working examples of this pattern (confirmed while auditing packets in this assignment, e.g. exp26-u11-012-q5's corrected version explicitly asks a controls-not-just-reaches question), just not yet formalized as its own family/objective.
gaps.missingQuestionFormatsOrCues: No new format needed (existing 'choice' and 'explain' types already carry this pattern elsewhere in the bank). The gap is a lack of a NAMED, deliberately designed family at U11 that isolates the cause-and-effect skill (predicting how a stated change to one actor's position or possession changes the learner's best option) as its own explicit objective, rather than the pattern appearing incidentally inside scenes built for other topics.
gaps.developmentalRationale: Hockey Canada's Vision & Scanning principles describe 'updating the read after pressure moves' as a coachable skill in its own right, not just a byproduct of scanning drills. U11 sits developmentally between the pure-observation U7/U9 bands and the heavier tactical-system content that begins at U13 -- a good bridge point to make prediction-under-change an explicit, named skill before it gets folded into more complex team-system content.

gaps.skillConcept: Match a defender to a changing threat with an explicit switch cue (distinct from the many existing single-freeze coverage scenes)

U13 has 50 scenarios / 400 questions and the largest topic count (45) of any age band, with many single-scenario coverage topics already (confirmed via topicRows: most U13 defensive topics show exactly 1 scenario each, by the bank's normal 1:1 granularity) -- but per this gap plan's own caveat, that 1-scenario-per-topic pattern is NOT itself evidence of a gap. The genuine gap is the ABSENCE of any scene built around an explicit mid-scene coverage handoff/switch as the stated objective (distinct from this assignment's audited exp26b-u18-004-q5, which tests STICKING to an assignment, the opposite skill).

gaps.developmentalRationale: IIHF's 3v3 coaching resource and Hockey Canada's downloads both name defensive-assignment switching as an age-appropriate U13+ concept; pairing this gap with the already-audited 'stick to your confirmed assignment' pattern (exp26b-u18-004-q5) gives the bank both halves of the same coaching principle at appropriate ages.
gaps.recommendedSmallPilot: 2 new U13 scenes (4 questions), each with three attackers/defenders and one explicit, coach-stated switch cue, asking which defender should now cover which attacker.
